steps.say: Kawasaki disease is diagnosed at the bedside, not in the laboratory. Classic disease needs fever for at least 5 days plus 4 of 5 features: bilateral non exudative conjunctivitis, oral changes with strawberry tongue and cracked lips, polymorphous rash, extremity changes with later peeling, and cervical lymphadenopathy over 1.5 centimetres. The lips, tongue, eyes, rash, hands, and nodes together make the diagnosis.
steps.tx: The **classic diagnostic criteria** require fever for at least **5 days** plus **4 of 5** features: bilateral **non exudative bulbar conjunctivitis**, **oral changes** with strawberry tongue and cracked red lips, **polymorphic rash**, **extremity changes** with erythema and periungual desquamation, and **cervical lymphadenopathy** over **1.5 cm**. No single test confirms the disease, so the criteria plus raised inflammatory markers carry the diagnosis.

vis.alt: Composite image showing a child with strawberry tongue, bilateral conjunctivitis, polymorphous rash, and peeling fingertips characteristic of Kawasaki disease.
vis.caption: Key clinical features of Kawasaki disease in children. Image: Dong Soo Kim, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: Babies under 6 months often show too few features to meet the classic count, yet their coronaries are at greatest risk. In unexplained fever lasting 7 days or more, incomplete disease is investigated with CRP of 30 milligrams per litre or higher and ESR of 40 millimetres per hour or higher plus supplemental laboratory and echo criteria. Waiting for the full picture in these infants invites aneurysms.
steps.tx: **Incomplete Kawasaki disease** threatens infants under **6 months** with unexplained fever for **7 days** or more who lack the full criteria. Investigation uses **CRP 30 mg/L** or higher and **ESR 40 mm/hr** or higher with supplemental anaemia, platelet, albumin, liver enzyme, and urine criteria, and echocardiography decides treatment when the laboratory algorithm points toward the disease.

vis.alt: Diagnostic flowchart for incomplete Kawasaki with aneurysmal coronaries and echocardiogram inset.
vis.caption: Incomplete disease earns IVIG by algorithm with echo deciding the rest. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Immunoglobulin transforms the outlook when given early. A single infusion of 2 grams per kilogram over 10 to 12 hours within the first 10 days of fever cuts coronary aneurysm risk from 25 percent to under 4 percent. The infusion should never be delayed for test results when the clinical diagnosis is firm.
steps.tx: **First-line IVIG therapy** is a single **2 g/kg** infusion over **10-12 hours** within **10 days** of fever onset, reducing coronary aneurysm risk from **25%** to under **4%**. Treatment within the first 10 days with aspirin remains effective even after day 10 when inflammation persists, and the diagnosis alone justifies infusion without awaiting echocardiography.

vis.alt: Classic Kawasaki diagnostic criteria with potential coronary artery complications.
vis.caption: Five principal features with persistent fever define complete disease. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Aspirin has two different roles across the illness. High dose aspirin at 30 to 50 milligrams per kilogram per day controls fever and inflammation until the child is afebrile for 48 hours, then low dose aspirin at 3 to 5 milligrams per kilogram per day prevents clots until 6 to 8 weeks after onset. Other anti inflammatory drugs must not replace it.
steps.tx: **Aspirin dosing in KD** starts high at **30-50 mg/kg/day** in divided doses through the febrile phase, then steps down to antiplatelet **3-5 mg/kg/day** once afebrile for **48 hours**, continuing until **6-8 weeks** post onset with normal coronaries. Long term aspirin users need annual influenza vaccination against Reye syndrome, with a substitute antiplatelet during chickenpox or influenza exposure.

steps.say: Coronary size is judged against body surface area, not absolute millimetres alone. Dilation and small aneurysms are distinguished from medium disease by rising Z-score bands, while giant aneurysms are carrying the greatest threat of clots and later narrowing.
steps.tx: The **coronary artery Z-score criteria** standardise dimensions: dilation is **Z-score 2.0** to under **2.5**, small aneurysm **2.5** to under **5.0**, medium aneurysm **5.0** to under **10.0**, and giant aneurysm **Z-score 10.0** or above or absolute lumen **8 mm** or wider. Serial echocardiography at diagnosis, 2 weeks, and 6 to 8 weeks tracks these scores, and giant lesions earn lifelong anticoagulation with activity limits.

points: Giant means Z-score 10.0 or lumen 8 mm or wider
Highest risk of thrombosis and stenosis
right.title: Giant Aneurysms

steps.say: Persistent fever after immunoglobulin is defining resistance. Persistent or recrudescent fever beyond thirty six hours after the first infusion ends is marking IVIG resistant disease, seen in ten to twenty percent of cases. These children carry higher aneurysm risk and must step up to second line therapy without delay.
steps.tx: The **IVIG-resistance definition** is persistent or recrudescent fever at **36 hours** or beyond after completing the first IVIG infusion, occurring in **10-20%** of cases. Risk scores combining young age, high neutrophils, low platelets, and raised liver enzymes flag likely resistance early, and such children merit closer echo surveillance plus readiness to escalate treatment.

nodes.label: First IVIG infusion completes over 10-12 hours with aspirin cover
Temperature watched for 36 hours after the infusion ends
Fever persisting at 36 hours defines resistant disease in 10-20%
Second line therapy starts at once to protect the coronaries

steps.say: Resistant disease has three proven escape routes. A second dose of immunoglobulin at two grams per kilogram, high dose methylprednisolone pulses at thirty milligrams per kilogram per day for three days, or infliximab at five milligrams per kilogram are rescuing most children. Corticosteroids are also front loading severe cases with shock or very young age.
steps.tx: **Second-line therapy for resistant KD** offers a second IVIG dose at **2 g/kg**, high dose intravenous **methylprednisolone** pulses at **30 mg/kg/day** for **3 days**, or **infliximab** at **5 mg/kg**. Choice follows severity and contraindications, anakinra covers refractory cases in specialist hands, and repeat echocardiography after rescue confirms whether the coronary Z-scores have stabilised.

steps.say: Immunoglobulin borrows immunity that blocks live vaccines for months. Measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella vaccines must wait 11 months after high dose IVIG because passive antibodies neutralise the vaccine viruses. Inactivated vaccines stay on schedule, and any measles exposure in the gap needs preventive immunoglobulin.
steps.tx: **Vaccine delay after IVIG** postpones live viral vaccines including measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella for **11 months** after high dose administration, since passive antibodies blunt the vaccine response. Inactivated vaccines proceed normally, exposed unprotected children receive passive prophylaxis, and the primary care record must flag the deferred live vaccine dates.

points: Live vaccines wait 11 months after IVIG
Flag deferred dates in the vaccine record
left.title: Live Vaccines Deferred

points: Exposure gaps covered by passive prophylaxis
right.title: Inactivated Vaccines Continue
